criterion: A journal month that cannot be read is reported by doctor rather than skipped in silence
summary: Reviewer built eleven journal-directory states by hand and compared both trees: a FIFO month, a chmod 000 month, a directory named like a month, a dangling symlink, an AF_UNIX socket, a month truncated past the size bound, a directory whose mode makes lstat fail on two perfectly good months, two readable months, and an empty directory. Every one that was silent before is named now, with no false positive on the readable pair. skipped_months never raised in any case, including when glob itself failed, and leaked no descriptor - /dev/fd counted before and after each call, delta +0 every time, including twelve readable months. Cost measured rather than assumed: flat at about 0.33ms because it is O(months) with a retention bound of six, which is 0.18% of doctor's runtime on a 20,000-record journal and is paid only by a human-invoked diagnostic. Two residual silences found, both confirmed pre-existing and both outside this criterion's wording: a journal directory at chmod 000 makes glob raise so the entire history disappears with no warning at all, and names that do not match MONTH_NAME are read by nothing and named by nothing. One LOW accuracy nit: when lstat raises, the reason reads 'not a plain file' for files that are plain.
